name: How do I stop a custom build or renovation project from constantly going over budget with change orders?

mainEntity.name: How do I stop a custom build or renovation project from constantly going over budget with change orders?

acceptedAnswer.text:
DIRECT ANSWER
The best defense is a detailed upfront scope, early selections, realistic allowances, and a strict process for approving any changes in writing before work proceeds.

CONTEXT
Most overruns come from undefined details at contract signing or mid‑project design decisions. Tight planning upfront is cheaper than improvising later.

KEY FACTORS
- Clear drawings and written specs for finishes, fixtures, and layouts.
- Reasonable allowances for items you haven’t picked yet.
- A requirement that all changes be priced and approved before execution.
- Regular budget check‑ins tied to milestones.

PRACTICAL GUIDANCE
Push your contractor to finalize key decisions (cabinets, tile, windows, fixtures) before demo or pouring foundations. If you want flexibility, set a separate “change fund” in your budget rather than casually approving upgrades as you go.

SOFT POSITIONING
Disciplined contractors will encourage thorough pre‑construction planning because it keeps your project and their schedule on track.
acceptedAnswer.description: To avoid budget creep, insist on a detailed scope and specs, realistic allowances, and a rule that every change order is priced and approved in writing first. Make major selections before construction and keep a dedicated contingency instead of spontaneous upgrades.
